overview: Fiji is an island country in the South Pacific, made up of more than 300 islands. Its capital and largest city, Suva, is on the main island of Viti Levu. Fiji became independent from the United Kingdom in 1970. Most Fijians are either Indigenous Fijians or Indo-Fijians, whose ancestors came from India, and rugby is the national sport.

geography.text: Most people live on the two largest islands, Viti Levu and Vanua Levu, which are volcanic and mountainous, with rainforest on their wetter eastern sides. Many of the smaller islands are coral islands surrounded by reefs. Fiji lies in the path of tropical cyclones.

history.text: Fiji was settled about 3,000 years ago by the Lapita people. Its chiefs gave the islands to Britain in 1874, and the British brought workers from India to work on sugar plantations. Fiji became independent in 1970, and tensions between Indigenous Fijians and Indo-Fijians led to several coups between 1987 and 2006.

events.title: Coups
events.text: The first of several military coups takes place.

government.text: Fiji is a parliamentary republic. Parliament elects the President, and the Prime Minister leads the government. Fiji had four coups between 1987 and 2006, partly because of tensions between Indigenous Fijians and Fijians of Indian descent. Elections returned in 2014.

economy.text: Tourism is the biggest industry, along with sugar, bottled water, fish and timber. Money sent home by Fijians working abroad, including soldiers in UN peacekeeping missions, is also important.

culture.text: Fijian culture blends Indigenous Melanesian traditions with those of Indo-Fijians, whose ancestors came from India to work on sugar plantations. Kava, a drink made from a pepper plant root, is shared at ceremonies. Fiji has more than 300 islands.

items.title: Kava ceremony
items.text: A drink shared to welcome guests and mark important events.

items.title: Fire walking
items.text: A ceremony on Beqa island where men walk across hot stones.

sport.text: Rugby is Fiji's national passion. Its sevens team won the first ever Olympic rugby gold in 2016, Fiji's first Olympic medal of any kind, and won again in 2020. Fijian players star in professional rugby around the world.

items.title: Vijay Singh
items.text: The golfer was world number one in 2004.

didYouKnow: Fiji is made up of about 330 islands.
